card. The sponsor is the person affiliated with the DoD or other Federal agency who took responsibility for verifying and authorizing the applicant's need for an ID card. Applicants for a CAC must be sponsored by a DoD government official or employee. Sponsorship and enrollment information on the ID card applicant shall be entered in DEERS prior to issuance.

(3) Background investigation. Background investigation is required for those individuals eligible for a CAC. A background investigation is required for those eligible for other forms of DoD ID cards. Sponsored CAC applicants shall not be required for those eligible for other forms of DoD ID cards. Sponsored CAC applicants shall not be required for those eligible for other forms of DoD ID cards. A CAC without a favorably adjudicated background investigation shall not be issued in FIPS Publication 201-3. Applicants that have been denied a CAC based on an unfavorable adjudication, or whose background investigation may submit an appeal in accordance with FIPS Publication 201-3 and Office of Personnel Management Memorandum, "Final Credentialing Standards for Issuing Personal Identity Verification (PIV) Cards under HSPD-12."

(4) Identity and eligibility verification. Identity and eligibility verification shall be completed at a RAPIDS workstation. Eligibility verification shall inspect identity and eligibility documentation and RAPIDS shall authenticate that individuals are eligible. DoD ID cards are provided only to those sponsored and with a current affiliation with the DoD. RAPIDS can capture uniquely identifying characteristics that bind an individual to the identification maintained on the account with DEERS and to the ID card issued by RAPIDS. These characteristics may include, but are not limited to, digital photographs and fingerprints.

(5) Issuance. ID cards shall be issued at the RAPIDS workstation after sponsorship, enrollment and identity and eligibility verification, background investigation (CAC only), and identity and eligibility verification requirements have been satisfied.

(6) Use and maintenance. ID cards shall be used as proof of identity and DoD affiliation to facilitate access to DoD facilities and systems. Additionally, ID cards shall represent authorization to obtain benefits and privileges in accordance with DoD policies.

(7) Retrieval and revocation. ID cards shall be retrieved by the sponsor or sponsoring organization when the ID card has expired, when it is damaged or decommissioned, or when the cardholder is no longer affiliated with the DoD or no longer meets the eligibility requirements for the card. The active status of the DEERS and RAPIDS infrastructure and the PK certificates on the CAC shall be revoked.

(b) The guidelines and restrictions of this paragraph apply to all forms of DoD ID cards.

(1) Any person willfully altering, damaging, looting, counterfeiting, or using these cards in an unauthorized manner is subject to fine or imprisonment as both, as prescribed in 18 U.S.C. 489, 506, 509, 701, and 1001. Section 701 of 18 U.S.C. prohibits counterfeiting or counterfeiting DoD ID cards in an unauthorized manner, under penalty of fine or imprisonment, as both. Unauthorized use of ID cards would exist if bearers used the card to obtain benefits and privileges to which they are not entitled. Examples include photocopying the DoD ID card to facilitate medical care processing, check processing, cash checking, tax verifying, etc. Compliance with 51 U.S.C. appendix 501 (also known as "The Service member's Civil Relief Act"), administration of other military related benefits to eligible beneficiaries. When possible, the ID card will be electronically authenticated in lieu of photographing the card.

(2) International agreements (including cease-fire of forces agreement) and host-nation law may limit and define the types of supervise available to DoD personnel in overseas areas. An ID card may be used to verify eligibility in the United States for access, for example, commissary or exchange facilities, the use of such facilities overseas may be limited to persons stationed or performing temporary duty in a foreign country under official orders in support of a mutual defense mission with the host nation.
